MID-STAGE FIRE WOLF, working name SMOULDERPUP, between a humble Cindercub wolf pup and a majestic fire-crowned Blazefang. Orange/russet coat, pale muzzle/chest blaze, dark orange spots, clear canine muzzle, modest triangular ears. Lanky adolescent with substantial paws slightly too large for its developing body; a heavy uneven ruff clumps around neck and shoulders like a crown that has not opened yet. Only two or three BANKED EMBER seams inside the ruff, not flames; the coat smoulders quietly. A scruffy tail plume beginning to uncurl. The middle must feel transitional and charmingly awkward but healthy, not malformed or ill. No spectacular fire crown yet, no fire on feet/tail, no wings or armour. A wolf learning to carry its heat, same individual as the pup.

MID-STAGE RIVER REPTILE, working name RIVERWISP, between the curious blue lizard Ripplet and a spectacular serpentine Tidewyrm. Blue #3a8fd8/teal, pale underside, pale rounded cheek sacs, recognisable ring markings. Long gangly lizard body with four webbed legs slightly too large for its body, still clearly walking on all four feet. A half-grown neck frill has broad folded floppy fin lobes, visible fin ribs, drooping close to shoulders; not yet a magnificent crest. A muscular paddle tail beginning to elongate, ring bands still readable. Awkward bank-and-river adolescent, grounded and healthy. Modest curious eyes, same face shape as a river lizard; not a fish, wolf, dinosaur or winged dragon. No water aura or levitation yet. Reserve the full wave crests and long flowing final silhouette.

MID-STAGE GROVE BOAR, working name THICKETBOAR, between the small moss-backed Mosshog and a spectacular walking-grove Thornback. A healthy burly shaggy brown boar, broad familiar snout, modest eyes and ears, substantial short legs, short tusks, stub tail, warm speckles. Its moss bed is overgrown and LOPSIDED: a few thin young woody saplings and uneven bramble shoots growing along its back, no full tree canopy. One small empty nest remains visible at the shoulder. The back vegetation feels half-organised like an adolescent garden; animal skeleton is healthy and symmetric, not broken. Keep readable boar outline under greenery. Reserve the final great tree and thorn crown, no antlers, armour, fairy ornaments or random flowers obscuring the face.

FINAL STAGE TIDEWYRM, an awe-inspiring river-reptile guardian evolved from the blue river lizard Ripplet through gangly Riverwisp. This remains the SAME lizard-derived individual, not a different animal. Spectacular new silhouette: long flowing serpentine trunk carried in one majestic S curve, four stout webbed legs still present, a thick muscular paddle tail, an enormous folded neck frill now fully opened into a crown of three broad curling WAVE FINS framing the head and shoulders. Broad lower dorsal fin carries the wave rhythm down the spine; no arbitrary spikes. Dark deep blue #14508f body, pale blue underside, cheek sacs and ring markings mature into recognisable band landmarks, modest calm eyes and recognisable blunt reptile face. A narrow clean arc of water curls beneath the tail and around the feet, visually suggesting command of currents; it must not obscure anatomy or form scenery. Powerful graceful guardian, not a fat crocodile with a fin glued on and not a winged dragon. No horns, wings or fur. The neck frill's final unfurling is the reward. Full body still grounded enough to assess contact points.

FINAL STAGE THORNBACK, the spectacular walking grove evolved from small moss-backed Mosshog through overgrown Thicketboar. The SAME brown BOAR remains clearly recognisable: broad snout, modest ears, small amber eyes, familiar speckled face, substantial four legs and boar tusks. New silhouette: a great low-branched living TREE rooted along the broad powerful back, two or three great rounded leafy crown masses spread like a shelter canopy, woody thorn crown integrated around shoulders, old small nest visible between the branch roots. Tree and animal are integrated living anatomy, not a boar standing in front of a forest. Whole boar plus entire canopy in frame. Deep cool greens #24503e #3f8558 and warm bark #4a3426 #8a6444, warm brown body. A few blossoms nestled in moss, no grass terrain below it. Animal body is the solid foundation; tall broad woodland canopy radically transforms its outline. Quiet protective presence, a little world the tamer has raised, not an angry monster. No humanoid/treefolk face or deer antlers.
